summary: Confirmed DONE (60633eff3). useTheme no longer has a mount effect. One module-level controller applies the theme on module load, through the setters and through one shared matchMedia/storage/registry listener set. The snapshot is cached and invalidated by events, custom-theme parsing is cached by the raw string, and the appearance sheet is moved and rewritten only when needed. ChatMarkdown and the other 7 consumer files now cost a subscription per mount, with no style rewrite, change event or forced style read. No other code path applies the theme per mount: the remaining applyAppearancePreferencesToDocument and applyThemeToDocument callers are user actions, environment changes or editor previews. The fix leaves one narrow behavioural gap compared with the old per-mount apply, described under fixDefects.

evidence.note: useTheme is useSyncExternalStore plus derived values only. The old per-consumer useEffect(() => applyTheme(theme), [theme]) (f1be4abc7 useTheme.ts:226-228) is gone.

The module-load applyThemeChange(getStored()) is the only apply that is not tied to a change. The module loads at boot for every route through the dynamic import in apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:377 (RootRouteView).

attachDocumentListeners installs one matchMedia, one storage and one registry listener per document on the first subscribe and keeps them for the document's lifetime. handleSystemColorSchemeChange (215) and handleThemeStorage (220) apply once rather than N times.
getSnapshot is cached via snapshotStale and invalidated by invalidateAndEmit, by subscribe, and by read-through while there are no listeners.
The transition guard does not force a synchronous reflow. syncBrowserChromeTheme runs in the next rAF on suppressed applies.

The textContent write is skipped when the text is unchanged. ensureAppearancePreferencesStyleElement (~745-752) moves the element only when it is not the last element in <head>. None of the lazy CSS chunks (projects, automations, pullRequests, overview, xterm) define :root vars that overlap the appearance sheet, so moving it less often changes nothing visible.

Parsed custom themes are cached by the raw stored string. setCustomThemes and setActiveThemeId (207, 250) notify subscribeThemeRegistry (219), so the cached snapshot stays correct for same-tab writes, including importThemeFromFile and the AppearanceSettings paths.

The browser test mounts 25 consumers and asserts 0 head mutations, 0 appearance events and 1 storage listener. A toggle produces exactly 1 appearance event and the guard lifts without a forced reflow.

The per-message consumer now only subscribes. The other useTheme consumers are ChatView, DiffPanel, DiffWorkerPoolProvider, PreviewPanel, FilesTab, SettingsPanels and AppearanceSettings, and none of them apply anything on mount.

Fix defect. The first-consumer catch-up only compares appliedTheme with the stored mode and the .dark class, so cross-tab changes to the active theme id, custom themes or appearance prefs made before the first consumer mounts are never applied. The old per-mount applyTheme picked them up.

fixDefects: One minor regression compared with the old per-mount apply. The document listeners are installed lazily on the first useTheme subscribe (useTheme.ts:269-273 -> attachDocumentListeners at 240). The catch-up at 253-261 only re-applies when the stored light/dark/system mode or the .dark class differs. The module loads at boot for every route, but routes such as Projects, Overview, the PR list and Automations mount no useTheme consumer. Suppose a tab has been on one of those routes since load and another tab changes ryco:active-theme, ryco:custom-themes or the appearance preferences. No storage listener exists yet, so nothing happens then. When the user later opens a chat (ChatView mounts useTheme), the catch-up sees the same mode and dark class and skips the apply. The tab keeps the old palette or appearance until a reload or the next real theme change. The old code re-applied on every mount, so it would have corrected this. Impact is very low because it needs a cross-tab change before the first consumer mount. Negligible leftovers: subscribe() sets snapshotStale = true even when the cache is already fresh, so each ChatMarkdown mount runs one readSnapshot (a few localStorage reads, one matchMedia query object, small array copies). This costs microseconds, not a style recalc. applyThemeToDocument (registry.ts:299-310) still rewrites identical theme text, and applyAppearancePreferencesToDocument still always dispatches its event, but both now run only on real changes.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening in apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts: install the document listeners together with the module-load apply, i.e. call attachDocumentListeners() inside the `if (typeof document !== "undefined" && hasThemeStorage())` block at line 174, right after applyThemeChange(getStored()). Keep the call in subscribe() so that re-attaching after __resetThemeControllerForTests still works. With listeners attached from boot, cross-tab and system changes are applied even on routes without a consumer, and the catch-up comparison at 253-261 can stay as a safety net or be removed. Optionally, in subscribe() only set snapshotStale = true when listeners.length was 0 before the push, which drops the per-mount readSnapshot. Test: extend themeController.browser.tsx to load the module with no consumer mounted, dispatch a StorageEvent for ryco:active-theme with a non-default theme id stored, and assert that the #ryco-active-theme style element appears. Run the focused browser test with bun run --cwd apps/web test:browser -- themeController.
decisionReason: Web-only theme controller change. It does not touch auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle ownership or the Hub protocol.
